clue.text: One of the provisions may be a late amendment

indicators.note: an amendment alters a text, so these three words are reworked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone suggests a change to the rules on supplies might be a late amendment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amendment' rearranges BE A LATE; 'may' only links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Provisions are food supplies, and anything edible counts as one of them.

clue.text: Cuts a nice design for such a tile

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective describing this kind of tile

indicators.note: a design arranges elements into a pattern, so these letters are laid out afresh

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A craftsman cuts a pleasing pattern into a decorative tile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'design' rearranges CUTS A NICE. The answer is an adjective, so 'such a tile' means a tile of this kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Encaustic work has coloured clays or pigments burnt into the surface, as on medieval floor tiles.

clue.text: He gives health to Daisy

parts.note: to give someone's health is to drink to them, so this is a person raising a glass to a friend named Daisy

explanation.walkthrough: It looks like a doctor curing a patient, but 'gives health' is the toast 'your health!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who proposes a drink in honour of another person is said to give their health.

clue.text: The best judo body-hold

definitions.meaning: the top grade in judo, marked by the colour of the sash
a strap that holds round the body, a waistband

explanation.definitionFit: The dark sash marks a judo expert's highest grades, and a strap round the waist holds the body.

clue.text: Hairy type from eastern parts of USA

parts.note: E is the standard abbreviation for east or eastern

indicators.note: the word is broken into parts and put back in another order

explanation.surface: A shaggy fellow comes from the eastern parts of America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts of' splits up the country's letters; Esau is the hairy brother of Jacob in Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis Jacob's brother is described as a hairy man, unlike smooth-skinned Jacob.

clue.text: Hopeless condition the French mate

parts.note: des is a French plural article form, 'of the' or 'some'
to mate is to pair, as animals do

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's partner finds herself in a hopeless state.
explanation.definitionFit: Despair is utter loss of hope, a state in which nothing seems possible.

clue.text: No satisfaction if record number put up marquee

parts.note: a gramophone record is a disc

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting a word up means reading it from bottom to top

parts.note: a marquee is a large tent

explanation.surface: Organisers are unhappy when a record crowd means a marquee must go up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' applies only to the number in this down entry; 'if' merely links. 'marquee' is the tent, not a grand event.
explanation.definitionFit: Discontent is a lack of contentment, the dissatisfied feeling of wanting things otherwise.

clue.text: Flay king lizard

parts.note: to flay is to strip off the hide, to skin
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A command to strip the hide from a royal reptile.
explanation.definitionFit: Skinks are a large family of smooth-scaled, short-legged reptiles.

clue.text: Break down proceeds of any sale

indicators.note: what proceeds from these words is a fresh arrangement of their letters

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An accountant must itemise the takings from any sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'proceeds of' looks like money from a sale; it signals rearranging ANY SALE.
explanation.definitionFit: To examine something by separating it into its parts is to break it down.

clue.text: Rebuked renegade of French rising

parts.note: a rat is someone who deserts their side

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: de is French for of

explanation.surface: A traitor of the French uprising was reprimanded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' applies only to the French word, read upwards in this down entry. 'rated' is an old verb for scolding.
explanation.definitionFit: To rate someone is an old verb meaning to scold or berate them angrily.

clue.text: She gives a small volume to academic associate

parts.note: cl is the abbreviation for centilitre, a small volume
ARA stands for Associate of the Royal Academy

explanation.surface: A woman hands over a slim book to a fellow scholar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gives a ... to' is linking: CL is followed by ARA. 'volume' suggests a book but is a measure of liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: Clara is a woman's given name, so it stands for a female person.

clue.text: Attacker to fool Italian losing head in riot

parts.note: an ass is a foolish person

indicators.note: letters in a riot are thrown into disorder
the word drops its first letter, its head

parts.note: taken as the word itself before its first letter goes

explanation.surface: A thug sets out to make a fool of an Italian during a disturbance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' drops the first letter of the nationality, then 'in riot' rearranges what is left (giving AILANT).
explanation.definitionFit: An assailant is someone who attacks another person, especially physically.

clue.text: Raising apprehension

definitions.meaning: grasping an idea, quickness to understand

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the act of taking up or lifting and the mental grasp of a point, as in 'quick on the' it.

clue.text: In vulgar speech, man observed to be soused

parts.note: cock is a familiar, slangy way to address a man, as in 'wotcher, cock'
to eye is to watch, so observed is eyed

explanation.surface: A coarse speaker is seen to be drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' links the wordplay to the definition. COCK is a working-class British form of address for a man, like 'mate'.
explanation.definitionFit: Soused is slang for drunk, and cockeyed has the same informal sense of tipsy.

clue.text: Lady artist got up to give drink to a bird

parts.note: she refers to a woman or lady

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting up means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist
to water an animal is to give it drink

explanation.surface: A woman painter rises to offer refreshment to a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got up' reads the artist upwards in this down entry; 'to' links the wordplay to the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Shearwaters are long-winged seabirds that skim low over the waves.

clue.text: As a rule taking quarters in Rugby

definitions.text: As a rule taking quarters in Rugby

parts.words: As a rule taking quarters in Rugby
parts.note: the number in the arithmetic 'rule of' it, and also the number taken with quarters to name the backs in rugby

explanation.walkthrough: 'As a rule' sounds like 'usually' but means the 'rule of three'; rugby's backs are the 'three-quarters'.
explanation.definitionFit: The rule of three is a proportion method, and rugby's three-quarters are the backs between half-backs and full-back.

clue.text: Achievement of broody hen?

parts.note: a broody hen's achievement would be hatching her eggs, but achievement is also the heraldic term for a coat of arms

explanation.walkthrough: In heraldry an 'achievement' is a full display of arms; the answer is a diamond-shaped funeral display of one, which looks like a hen's 'hatching'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hatchment is a diamond-shaped tablet bearing a dead person's coat of arms, a heraldic achievement.

clue.text: Vocal offering of mountain goat?

parts.note: a male goat up a mountain would be a ..., and this is also a style of country song

explanation.walkthrough: A billy is a male goat, so a goat on a mountain is a 'hill billy' in the pun; the word also names rural folk music from the Appalachians.
explanation.definitionFit: Hillbilly music is the old American name for rural country songs from the mountains of the South.

clue.text: Figure-head to ease, say, state of USA

parts.note: ten is a number, a figure
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken, so its sound counts

parts.note: the word ease sounds like the plural of the letter E

explanation.surface: A leading figure tries to calm one American state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' links. NESS is a headland, and 'say' makes 'ease' the letters EE, its sound being 'Es'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennessee is one of the fifty United States, its capital Nashville.

clue.text: Force to study the line

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
a strain is a line of descent, a breed or lineage

explanation.surface: A trainee is pushed to learn the company line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the' links. 'line' looks like a line of text to study; it is a lineage.
explanation.definitionFit: To constrain someone is to compel or oblige them, to force them.

clue.text: Beginning climb north to the top

indicators.note: in a down clue, the piece goes to the top, above the climb

parts.note: an ascent is a climb

explanation.surface: A climber begins heading north towards the summit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the top' puts N above ASCENT in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nascent is just coming into being, at its beginning stage.

clue.text: Dog gives tongue — this one?

parts.note: a hound gives tongue by barking, but 'dog' before a language name means a debased form of it, and tongue means language

explanation.walkthrough: Hounds 'give tongue' when they bay. 'Dog' prefixed to the language gives mock or crude classical language.
explanation.definitionFit: Dog Latin is crude, ungrammatical imitation of the classical language of ancient Rome.

clue.text: Quite tiddly with Los Angeles drink

indicators.note: tiddly means slightly drunk, so the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone gets quite merry drinking in Los Angeles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tiddly' (tipsy) scrambles the first word, giving TEQUI; Los Angeles is simply added.
explanation.definitionFit: Tequila is a Mexican spirit distilled from the blue agave plant.

clue.text: Clean kitchen vessel with panhandles here in USA

definitions.note: Panhandles are narrow strips of a state; Oklahoma and Texas have them

parts.note: to dust is to clean by wiping
a bowl is a kitchen container for mixing

explanation.surface: Cleaning a pan with handles in an American kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' links. 'panhandles' suggests pan handles in the kitchen but refers to the Oklahoma and Texas panhandles, worst hit by the 1930s drought.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1930s drought region of the southern Great Plains took in the Texas and Oklahoma panhandles.

clue.text: Gulls used originally to circle park

indicators.note: these letters go round the other piece
the word is set back to an earlier, different order of its letters

parts.note: P is the map abbreviation for park

explanation.surface: Gulls that once flew in circles round the park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' rearranges USED to DUES; 'to circle' puts that round P. 'Gulls' looks like birds but is a verb or plural noun for victims.
explanation.definitionFit: Gulls are people easily fooled, the victims of a con.

clue.text: Ruth left scene of chaos

parts.note: Babe Ruth was the famous American baseball player

explanation.surface: Ruth departed from a chaotic place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruth' looks biblical, but it is the American baseball star Babe Ruth.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical tower where languages were confused gives its name to any noisy confusion.

clue.text: Device used by RA everywhere

definitions.meaning: the motto of the Royal Artillery, RA, a heraldic device
the Latin word for in every place

explanation.definitionFit: The Royal Artillery's motto is a Latin word meaning 'in all places'.

clue.text: Roguish sort of angel?

definitions.meaning: a chief kind of angel, as in the prefix of archangel

explanation.definitionFit: The word means slyly playful, and as a prefix it makes a chief angel.

clue.text: John holds by the minister

indicators.note: one word holds the other within it

parts.note: Prester John was a legendary Christian king of the East
taken as written

explanation.surface: John is held in place by the clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' puts one word inside the legendary medieval priest-king's title.
explanation.definitionFit: A presbyter is an elder or priest in a church, a minister of religion.

clue.text: Joints secured by girder at start of job?

definitions.text: Joints secured by girder at start of job?

parts.words: Joints secured by girder at start of job?
parts.note: joints of meat, but also the body parts one girds before work in the biblical phrase about girding up

explanation.walkthrough: 'girder' looks like a steel beam but is someone girding up, as in 'gird up your loins' before a task.
explanation.definitionFit: Loins are cuts of meat from the back, and the lower body one girds before work.

clue.text: He squares the account with a final argument

definitions.meaning: one who pays off what is owed
a clinching point that ends a debate

explanation.definitionFit: The word names someone who pays a bill and also, colloquially, a decisive point that ends a dispute.

clue.text: Boat needing paint in Merseyside

definitions.note: the answer is a place in this English county

parts.note: a hoy is a small coasting vessel
lake is a crimson pigment used in paint

explanation.surface: A boat needs repainting in Liverpool's region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing' links. Merseyside is the county around Liverpool in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoylake is a seaside town on the Wirral peninsula, in the county of Merseyside.
